methodological_rigor.justification: Cell-line-based mechanistic study using two DLBCL cell lines (OCI-LY10, U2932) with reactive hyperplastic lymph node tissues as comparators, plus a small tissue comparison of 20 DLBCL patient samples vs healthy donors. Weaknesses: comparison of DLBCL cell lines to reactive hyperplastic lymph node tissues is not a matched comparator (different tissue compositions confound methylation/expression measures), no primary DLBCL cell validation, no in vivo validation (acknowledged as a limitation), use of MSP (semi-quantitative) rather than bisulfite sequencing or pyrosequencing for quantitative methylation. Patient cohort (n=20 DLBCL) mentioned but ZNF382 expression comparison is reported as 0.1236 vs 0.0211 without 95% CIs. Statistical methods (ANOVA with Newman-Keuls post-hoc, t-tests, n=3 biological replicates) are basic and appropriate in scale but no multiplicity correction or power calculation.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Preclinical cell-line study (Oxford 5). Clinical relevance is plausible but distant: ZNF382 is proposed as a tumor suppressor silenced by promoter hypermethylation in DLBCL, and DAC demethylation rescues expression and induces apoptosis. Hypomethylating agents (DAC, azacytidine) already have clinical use in DLBCL settings (cited phase I R-CHOP+CC-486), but the paper does not demonstrate DLBCL-specific clinical benefit or validate ZNF382 in primary patient samples functionally. Translational path is suggestive rather than demonstrated.

reporting_quality.justification: Standard preclinical cell-line reporting without a single applicable checklist (ARRIVE would apply if in vivo data were present; none are). Cell-line sources are identified (Shanghai Yu Bo Biotech), reagents and catalog numbers are provided, primer sequences are in Table 1, and assay details (DAC concentrations, timepoints, MSP cycling) are generally complete. Biological replicates (n=3) are specified. Gaps: no power calculation, no description of randomization/blinding for in vitro experiments, UCSC Genome Browser link redacted, and no data/code availability statement. Limitations are briefly acknowledged (no in vivo, no primary DLBCL cells).

novelty_literature.justification: Authors' prior clinical work (ref 4, 2024) established that low ZNF382 protein expression in DLBCL pathology samples correlates with poor prognosis. ZNF382 has been previously characterized as a tumor suppressor silenced by CpG methylation in gastric (Pei 2018), esophageal (Zhang 2018), and hepatocellular carcinoma (Dang 2019). The present study extends this paradigm to DLBCL cell lines with DAC rescue experiments and phenotypic assays (proliferation, migration, colony formation, apoptosis). This is a meaningful extension (first demonstration in DLBCL cell lines) rather than a conceptual advance.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is readable with clear section structure and figures described in detail. Some redundancy between results and discussion regarding the DAC dose-response findings. Reporting of effect sizes is mixed: some comparisons include p-values without means or CIs. Figures are explained in legends. Discussion appropriately contextualizes findings and speculates on mechanisms (including the 4 uM DAC anomaly attributed to apoptosis-induced mRNA degradation). Overall presentation is adequate.

key_strengths: Integrated epigenetic-functional workflow in DLBCL cell lines (MSP + RT-PCR + DAC rescue + ZNF382 overexpression + apoptosis/proliferation/migration/colony assays)
Extension of known ZNF382-tumor-suppressor paradigm from solid tumors to DLBCL cell lines
Consistent direction of effect across multiple phenotypic assays supporting tumor-suppressor function
Cell-line authentication source and reagents disclosed
key_concerns: Reactive hyperplastic lymph node tissue is a questionable comparator for DLBCL cell lines due to cell-composition differences; more appropriate would be matched germinal-center B cells
MSP is semi-quantitative; no bisulfite sequencing/pyrosequencing or methylation array validation
No in vivo validation (acknowledged) and no primary DLBCL cell testing
Small patient tissue cohort (n=20) with limited clinical annotation and no prognostic correlation in this study (relies on prior authors' work)
No sample-size or power justification, basic statistical framework without multiplicity correction
chief_reviewer.rationale: A coherent but limited preclinical cell-line study extending a known tumor-suppressor paradigm to DLBCL without in vivo or primary-cell validation; best fit is a lower-tier specialty journal after major revisions strengthening comparators, methylation quantification, and patient-sample linkage.
